audit.whatIsWrong: The page calls Playful / Trickster his ULTIMATE and writes it '(R)' in multiple places, saying it 'isn't unlocked yet' before 6.
audit.why: Playful / Trickster is Fizz's E — 16/14/12/10/8, available from level 3, untargetable during the hop, and it also grounds and slows. His actual ultimate is Chum the Waters, 120/100/80, which slows, then knocks up, and carries the grounding flag — that is what denies LeBlanc's Distortion return, and the page never mentions it at all.
audit.corrected: Playful named as his E with its real cooldowns; Chum the Waters named as the level-6 spike and as the tool that grounds your return.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer read 'Skill' on all seven rows while content win[] read LeBlanc x4 then Fizz x3.
audit.why: The packet levelChart and the content layer already agree with each other and with 50.6% over 2587 games: LeBlanc owns the ranged early rows, Fizz takes over from level 6 once Chum the Waters can hold her still.
audit.corrected: phases[0..3].side -> LeBlanc, phases[4..6].side -> Fizz, ratings adjusted, and the three flipped whys rewritten so no row argues with its sentence.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every spike hung on 'his ultimate' being the hop, so the actual level-6 power spike was missing.
audit.why: Fizz's 6 adds a 120s point-and-click-ish shark that slows, grounds, and knocks up — that is the spike that flips the lane, not the E he has had since 3.
audit.corrected: spikes[1] and spikes[3] rewritten; phases[4..6].why re-keyed to Chum the Waters and to Playful reaching 8s.

audit.why: Playful 16s->8s, Chum the Waters 120s->80s, Urchin Strike 8s->6s and your own 15s Distortion are the whole timing game.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with real numbers, and with the E/R slot correction folded in.

audit.whatIsWrong: Seastone Trident's auto-attack reset was never mentioned.
audit.why: The brief flags it: his combo opens with an auto reset (3s at rank 5), so the wind-up is the cue to step back, not the ability cast.

audit.why: Lint findings plus the template sweep.

edits.before: Playful/Trickster is the whole matchup at level 6 — it makes him untargetable, dodges your entire burst combo, and lets him land a free counter-hit while you're mid-animation. If he plays it correctly (holding it until you commit R-E-Q-W), your combo whiffs and he gets to punish you back safely. You need to bait it out with a half-commit or wait for it to be down before going all-in, otherwise this trade favors him.

If he holds it until you commit, your string whiffs and he punishes you back safely; at 6 he adds Chum the Waters, 120s, which grounds your return. Bait the hop with a half-commit or wait out its 8-to-16 seconds before going all-in.

notes: BIGGEST DEFECT ON THE PAGE: Playful / Trickster was called Fizz's ULTIMATE and written '(R)' throughout, with advice built on it 'not being unlocked' before level 6. It is his E, available from level 3, 16s down to 8s. His ultimate is Chum the Waters (120/100/80), which was never mentioned anywhere — and it is the ability that matters most to LeBlanc, since its grounding denies the Distortion return. Chart: the full layer read 'Skill' on all seven rows while content win[] and the packet already agreed on LeBlanc x4 then Fizz x3; the side edits align the full layer, and no paired win[N] edits exist because win[] already holds those values.
